collections.title: Classical & Ancient Centers
collections.summary: The foundational centers of classical triangle geometry: the incenter, centroid, circumcenter, orthocenter, nine-point center, symmedian point, Gergonne, Nagel, Mittenpunkt, Spieker, Feuerbach, Fermat, isodynamic, Napoleon, and Clawson points.

collections.title: Euler Line Centers
collections.summary: Classical centers lying on the Euler line X_2 X_3, including the De Longchamps point, Schiffler point, Exeter point, far-out point, homothetic center of the orthic and tangential triangles, and the Euler infinity point.

collections.title: Power Points, Circle Similicenters & Named Centers
collections.summary: 2nd and 3rd power points, the Bevan point, Brocard midpoint, Kosnita point, and internal and external centers of similitude of the circumcircle, incircle, and nine-point circle.

collections.title: Isogonal & Isotomic Conjugates of Classical Centers
collections.summary: Isogonal conjugates (X_59–X_74) and isotomic and cross conjugates (X_75–X_97) of the classical centers X_1–X_58.

collections.title: Centers on the Circumcircle
collections.summary: Notable points on the circumcircle of ABC, including the Tarry point, Steiner point, anticomplementary, Feuerbach, Kiepert, and Jerabek antipodes, and centers derived from circumcircle mappings.

collections.title: Centers on the Nine-Point Circle & Orthic Centers
collections.summary: Points on the nine-point circle (X_113–X_139), centers of the Kiepert, Feuerbach, and Jerabek rectangular hyperbolas, and centers transferred to the orthic triangle.

collections.title: Derived Triangle Centers, Isoscelizers & Ajima-Malfatti Points
collections.summary: Complements, anticomplements, and classical centers evaluated on the medial, orthic, tangential, and excentral triangles, together with congruent isoscelizer, equal detour, and Ajima-Malfatti points.

collections.title: Ceva Conjugates
collections.summary: Perspectors of the cevian triangle of P and the anticevian triangle of Q (P-Ceva conjugates of Q) for classical triangle centers.

collections.title: Line Conjugates
collections.summary: Intersections of line PQ with the trilinear polar of the isogonal conjugate of P (P-line conjugates of Q).

collections.title: Isogonal Conjugates II & Hirst Inverses
collections.summary: Isogonal conjugates of centers X_115–X_248, together with cross conjugates and X_2-Hirst inverses.

collections.title: Isotomic Conjugates II
collections.summary: Isotomic conjugates of previously cataloged triangle centers, together with X_2-Hirst inverses and radical centers.

collections.title: Parry Circle, Morley/Yff Centers & Pedal Centroids
collections.summary: The Parry circle center, Morley trisector centers, Yff equal-parallelians, trisected-perimeter, and equilateral-cevian points, Kenmotu point, and centroids of pedal and cevian triangles.

collections.title: Euler Line Substitutions & Hirst Inverses
collections.summary: Centers lying on the Euler line generated by X_k-substitutions and Hirst inversions, followed by the Tixier point, Ajima-Malfatti radical center, and Evans perspectors.

collections.title: Vecten Square Centers & Isoscelizer Centers
collections.summary: Inner and outer Vecten points and square-associated centers (Vierkanten in een driehoek, X_485–X_495), harmonic conjugates, and isoscelizer-associated centers (X_503–X_510).

collections.title: Centers on the Line at Infinity & Vector Directions
collections.summary: Points on the line at infinity x + y + z = 0 (X_511–X_526, isogonal conjugates of circumcircle points), unit vector direction centers, and classical midpoints.

collections.title: Brocard Axis Circles & Gibert Centers
collections.summary: Centers on the Brocard axis X_3 X_6 whose circles cut equal chords on the sidelines of ABC (X_566–X_584), congruent shrunk insquares points, and centers contributed by Bernard Gibert (X_616–X_642).

collections.title: Crossdifferences & Trilinear Poles
collections.summary: Trilinear multipliers for the Kiepert and Yff parabolas, crossdifferences of classical centers, and trilinear poles of central lines.

collections.title: Even (p, q) Circumcircle Points
collections.summary: Even trigonometric (p, q) points on the circumcircle and line at infinity, paired with their isogonal conjugates.

collections.title: Odd o-(p, q) Circumcircle Points
collections.summary: Odd trigonometric o-(p, q) points on the circumcircle and line at infinity, paired with their isogonal conjugates.

collections.title: Hatzipolakis-Yiu Centers, Hirst Inverses & Crossdifferences
collections.summary: Hatzipolakis-Yiu points, the Yiu angle point (X_848), Kiepert hyperbola multipliers, Hirst inverses, and Euler line intercepts.

collections.title: Star-Named Centers, Ehrmann Points & Anticomplements
collections.summary: Star-named centers (Agena, Achernar, Algenib, Alcor), Ehrmann points, anticomplements, and midpoints of classical triangle centers.

collections.title: Classical Midpoints, Euler Intercepts & Cevapoints
collections.summary: Midpoints of classical centers, Euler line intercepts, collinearity intersections, cevapoints, and pure-angle trilinear centers.

collections.title: Cross Conjugates, Trilinear Squares & Euler-Circumcircle Intersections
collections.summary: Cross conjugates, trilinear squares and cubes of classical centers, and the intersections of the Euler line with the circumcircle (X_1113, X_1114).

collections.title: Morley-Taylor-Marr, Hofstadter, Ehrmann & Star Centers
collections.summary: Morley-Taylor-Marr centers, Hofstadter points, the Ehrmann congruent squares point (X_1144), Grebe triangle centers, and star-named points (Aldebaran, Algjebbah, Altair, Altais).

collections.title: Saragossa Points
collections.summary: 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Saragossa points (Q, Q', Q'') constructed from the cevian and circumcevian triangles of classical centers.

collections.title: Saragossa Conjugates, Sharygin Points & Lemoine Homothetic Center
collections.summary: Isogonal and isotomic conjugates of the Saragossa points, Sharygin points, and the Lemoine homothetic center (X_1285).

collections.title: Collings Transforms
collections.summary: Concurrence points on the circumcircle of the circumcircles of AB'C', A'BC', and A'B'C, where A'B'C' is the reflection of ABC in P.

collections.title: Moses Intersections, Circumcircle Inverses, Wernau Points & Similicenters
collections.summary: Moses orthocentroidal-Euler intersections, circumcircle inverses, 1st and 2nd Wernau points (X_1337, X_1338), and similicenters of the circumcircle, nine-point circle, orthocentroidal circle, and Brocard circle.

collections.title: Brisse Transforms, Rigby/Griffiths Points & Complementary Conjugates
collections.summary: Polynomial centers on the incircle generated by the Brisse transform (X_1354–X_1367), Rigby and Griffiths points, and complementary and anticomplementary conjugates.

collections.title: Beth Conjugates & Harmonic Conjugates
collections.summary: Fixed-point P-beth conjugates of P and harmonic conjugates along central lines.

collections.title: Johnson-Yff Circle, Perspectors & Star-Named Centers
collections.summary: The Johnson-Yff circle center, tangential-of-tangential perspectors, star-named centers (Bellatrix, Betelgeuse, Biham), and Napoleon and Fermat crosssums.

collections.title: Orthojoins, Moses Circle Centers & Star-Named Centers
collections.summary: Orthojoins H(X) — orthopoles of the trilinear polars of isogonal conjugates (X_1512–X_1568) — together with Moses circle similicenters and star-named centers (Capella, Caph, Cebalrai, Celaeno, Chertan, Chort).

collections.title: TCC-Perspectors & Tripolar Centroids
collections.summary: Perspectors of the tangential triangle and the circumcevian triangle of P (X_1601–X_1634), tripolar centroids (X_1635–X_1651), and Evans and Grinberg perspectors.

collections.title: Circle-Related Points
collections.summary: Internal and external centers of similitude among the circumcircle, incircle, nine-point circle, Brocard circle, 1st and 2nd Lemoine circles, Apollonius circle, and Bevan circle.

collections.title: Mimosa Transforms
collections.summary: Centers generated by the Mimosa transform M(X) of classical triangle centers.

collections.title: Inverse Mimosa Transforms & Aleph Conjugates
collections.summary: Inverse Mimosa transforms of classical triangle centers and aleph conjugates.

collections.title: Zosma Transforms
collections.summary: Isogonal conjugates of the inverse Mimosa transforms (Z(X)) of classical triangle centers.

collections.title: Bicentric Pairs PU(k) & Orthocorrespondents
collections.summary: Midpoints, crosssums, crossdifferences, trilinear poles, and trilinear products of bicentric pairs PU(k) (X_1908–X_1982), Vega transforms, and orthocorrespondents (X_1992–X_2000).

collections.title: Orthocorrespondents, Gallatly Circle & Euler-Vecten-Gibert Points
collections.summary: Orthocorrespondents of classical centers (X_2001–X_2006), similicenters and intersections of the Gallatly circle (X_2007–X_2040), and the six Euler-Vecten-Gibert points and harmonic conjugates (X_2041–X_2054).

collections.title: Orion Transforms, Circumcircle Inverses, PK/NK Transforms, Reflections & Kepler Points
collections.summary: Orion transforms OT(X) (X_2055–X_2065), Caroli and Cursa points, circumcircle inverses (X_2070–X_2080), PK and NK transforms (X_2081–X_2092), classical reflections (X_2093–X_2105), and Kepler points and their isotomic conjugates (X_2106–X_2119).

collections.title: Eigencenters & Eigentransforms
collections.summary: Eigentransforms ET(X) — eigencenters of the cevian triangles of classical centers — paired with their isogonal conjugates on the self-isogonal cubic Z(X) (X_2120–X_2143), followed by X_2-eigentransforms (X_2144–X_2147).

collections.title: Isotomic Conjugates (X_2-Isoconjugates) I
collections.summary: Isotomic conjugates (X_2-isoconjugates) of triangle centers X_5 through X_892.

collections.title: Isotomic Conjugates (X_2-Isoconjugates) II
collections.summary: Isotomic conjugates (X_2-isoconjugates) of triangle centers X_901 through X_2099.

collections.title: Circumcircle CIR(X) Points & Gibert-Simson Transforms
collections.summary: Circumcevian-eigentransform points CIR(X) on the circumcircle and their isogonal conjugates (X_2365–X_2393), followed by Gibert-Simson transforms GS(X) on the Simson cubic K010 (X_2394–X_2419) and their isogonal conjugates on K162 (X_2420–X_2445).

collections.title: Circle & Conic Intersections, Lemoine Inverses & Radical Centers I
collections.summary: Intersections of central lines with the incircle, Bevan circle, Steiner inellipse, and Steiner circumellipse, inverses in the 1st and 2nd Lemoine circles, and circle radical centers (X_2446–X_2520).

collections.title: Circle Similicenters, Radical Centers & Isoconjugates II
collections.summary: Similicenters and intersections involving the orthocentroidal, 2nd Brocard, Parry, and Gallatly circles (X_2521–X_2573), followed by isogonal and X_k-isoconjugates (X_2574–X_2593).

collections.title: Bicentric Pairs PU(68)–PU(85) & Golden Arbelos Points
collections.summary: Sums, differences, crosssums, crossdifferences, trilinear poles, and midpoints of bicentric pairs PU(68) through PU(85) (X_2594–X_2670), together with the 1st and 2nd Golden Arbelos points (X_2671–X_2676).

collections.title: Rigby-Simson RS(P, U) & Simson-Rigby SR(P, U) Points
collections.summary: Rigby-Simson orthopoles RS(P, U) where the Simson lines of circumcircle points P and U meet (X_2677–X_2686), and Simson-Rigby circumcircle points SR(P, U) whose Simson lines pass through RS(P, U) perpendicular to PU (X_2687–X_2770).

collections.title: Isogonal Conjugates of Simson-Rigby SR(P, U) Points
collections.summary: Points on the line at infinity formed as the isogonal conjugates of the Simson-Rigby circumcircle points X_2687–X_2770.

collections.title: Simson-Moses SM(P, U) Points & Conjugates
collections.summary: Simson-Moses circumcircle points SM(P, U) generated by isotomic conjugation of circumcircle pairs (X_2855–X_2868) and their isogonal conjugates on the line at infinity (X_2869–X_2882).

collections.title: Isogonal Conjugates with Respect to Special Triangles
collections.summary: Complementary (medial-isogonal), anticomplementary-isogonal, tangential-isogonal, and excentral-isogonal conjugates of classical triangle centers, together with trilinear and barycentric products.

collections.title: MacBeath Points, Dual Centers DC(X) / CD(X) & Central Line Intersections
collections.summary: The eight MacBeath points (X_2967–X_2974), circle radical centers (X_2975–X_2978), dual triangle mappings DC(X) and CD(X) (X_2979–X_2998), the Danneels-Bevan homothetic center (X_2999), and the Soddy-antiorthic intersection (X_3000).

collections.title: Central Line Intersections, Stevanović Points & T/G Mappings
collections.summary: Pairwise intersections of the Brocard, de Longchamps, Gergonne, Lemoine, Nagel, orthic, Soddy, and Fermat axes (X_3001–X_3019), the 4th–10th Stevanović points (X_3020–X_3026), antipodal circle mappings and complements (X_3027–X_3111), and Quang Tuan Bui's TgX and GtX mappings (X_3112–X_3118).

collections.title: Danneels Perspectors & X_i-Ceva Conjugates
collections.summary: Eric Danneels' parallel-cevian perspectors (X_3119–X_3126) and a systematic catalog of X_i-Ceva conjugates of classical and central points (X_3127–X_3217).

collections.title: Side-Swapping SS(a → bc) Points, Parabola Vertices & Morley Equilateral Triangles
collections.summary: Side-swapping transformations SS(a → bc), vertices of the inscribed Kiepert and Yff parabolas (X_3233–X_3234), reflections in X_1 (X_3241–X_3245), and centers and perspectors of the six equilateral triangles related to the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Morley triangles (X_3272–X_3283).

collections.title: Incircle Transforms T(U), Trigonometric Offset Points & Kiepert Cusps
collections.summary: Barycentric products of perpendicular directions (X_3310), incircle transforms T(U) lying on the incircle (X_3318–X_3328), Darboux-cubic reflections and conjugates (X_3341–X_3358), trigonometric phase-shifted centers cos/sin/sec/csc/tan/cot(A ± θ) (X_3364–X_3409), and the Brocard-Kiepert-Fermat cusps (X_3411–X_3414).

collections.title: Vertex Conjugates, Saragossa Points & Neuberg Cubic Intersections
collections.summary: U-vertex conjugates of X formed from circumcevian vertex triangles (X_3415–X_3458), 1st Saragossa points (X_3449–X_3454), X_5- and X_30-Ceva conjugates on the Neuberg cubic (X_3460–X_3488), and the 1st dilation center and its circumcircle inverse (X_3513–X_3514).

collections.title: Euler Line Intercepts & Named Geometric Centers
collections.summary: Euler line intercepts of central lines (X_3515–X_3552), together with the Dosa, Pappus, Moses circumcircle/infinity, Don Quixote, Beltrami-Euler, Beltrami-Parry, Myakishev conic, Dixit, Odehnal, and Liu points (X_3555–X_3601).

collections.title: Morley Cubics, Medial Homothetic Centers H(X; M, t) & Kirikami-Schiffler Points
collections.summary: Centers associated with the three Morley cubics K029–K031 (X_3602–X_3615), medial-triangle t-dilation homothetic centers H(X; M, t) and their isogonal conjugates H⁻¹(X; M, t) (X_3616–X_3637), Soddy-Gergonne, Kirikami, Alkaid, and Almach points (X_3638–X_3646), and Kirikami-Schiffler points KS(T) (X_3647–X_3662).

collections.title: Central Triangle Combos Xcom(T) I: Intouch, Extouch, Incentral & Hexyl Triangles
collections.summary: Combo centers X_k-com(T) evaluated on the intouch (X_3663–X_3677), extouch (X_3678–X_3719), incentral (X_3720–X_3728), excentral, tangential, 1st Brocard, and hexyl triangles (X_3729–X_3738), plus matrix-product combos n(incentral)*n(medial) and inverse-triangle combos (X_3739–X_3757).

collections.title: Central Triangle Combos Xcom(T) II: Parameterized T(f, g) & Euler Triangles
collections.summary: Combo centers X_k-com[T(f, g)] and X_k-com[Inverse(nT(f, g))] for parameterized central triangles (X_3758–X_3810), followed by combo centers on the 1st through 5th Euler triangles (X_3811–X_3861).

collections.title: Inverse Central Triangle Combos Xcom[Inverse(n(T))]
collections.summary: Perspectors of ABC and parameterized central triangles T(f, g) (X_3862–X_3867), inverse 3rd/4th/5th Euler triangle combos (X_3868–X_3910), and combos and inverse-triangle combos across the intouch, extouch, orthic, tangential, hexyl, Brocard, incentral, excentral, intangents, and extangents triangles (X_3911–X_4000).

families.title: Points on the circumcircle; mappings Λ and Ψ
p: Centers X(74), X(98)-X(112), and many others in ETC lie on the circumcircle. Mappings Λ and Ψ derived from such a point P for application to points X, are defined here: Λ(P,X) = isogonal conjugate of the point where line PX meets the line at infinity.
Let Y = Λ(P,X), let Q = isogonal conjugate of P, and let Y and Z be the points where line YQ meets the circumcircle;
then Ψ(P,X) = Z.

families.title: Points on the nine-point circle
p: Centers X(113)-X(139) lie on the nine-point circle.

Suppose that X is a point on the nine-point circle, and let X' be the reflection of X in the orthocenter, H. Then X is the anticenter of the cyclic quadrilateral ABCX'. Let H_A be the orthocenter of triangle BCX, Let H_B be the orthocenter of CAX, and let H_C be the orthocenter of triangle ABX. Then the quadrilateral HH_AH_BH_C is homothetic to and congruent to the cyclic quadrilateral ABCX', and X is the center of homothety. (Randy Hutson, 9/23/2011)

families.title: Ceva conjugates
p: Centers X(191)-X(236) are Ceva conjugates. (The P-Ceva conjugate of Q is the perspector of the cevian triangle of P and the anticevian triangle of Q.)

families.title: Line conjugates

families.title: Isoscelizer points: X(503)-X(510)
p: Centers X(503)-X(510), and also centers X(173), X(174), X(258), and X(351)-X(364) are associated with isoscelizers.
A line L_A perpendicular to the internal bisector line of A is an A-isoscelizer.. Suppose X is a point not on a sideline of ABC, and let
L(A,X) =the A-isoscelizer passing through X;
E(A,X) =L(A,X)∩AC;
F(A,X) =L(A,X)∩AB;
T(A,X) =the triangle wth vertices A, E(A,X), F(A,X);
H(A,X) =A-altitude of T(A,X);
D(A,X) =distance between E(A,X) and F(A,X);
X(A) =distance between E(A,X) and F(A,X);
Cyclically define L(B,X), E(B,X), . . . , X(B) and L(C,X), E(C,X), . . . , X(C).
Each center, X(503) to X(510), is defined by Peter Yff as the point X of concurrence of isoscelers satisfying certain conditions.
Geometer's Sketchpad sketches for centers X(503)-X(510) were contributed by Peter Moses, May 7, 2005.

families.title: Centers on the lines at infinity: X(511)-X(526)
p: In barycentric coordinates, the line at infinity, L, is the set of points X = x : y : z satisfying x + y + z = 0. The isogonal conjugate of L, given by a^2 y z + b^2 z x + c^2 x y = 0, is the circumcircle (e.g., X(98)-X(112)).
The collection of collinearities reported below for each of the centers on L comprises a family of parallel lines.

Barycentrics x: y : z (and trilinears) for X(30), X(511)-X(526), and many other triangle centers on L, are polynomials in (a,b,c). For example, barycentrics for X(511) are p(a,b,c) : p(b,c,a) : p(c,a,b), where

Such polynomials comprise a family that can be partitioned into two subfamilies: even and odd. Each subfamily can be generated as linear combination of polynomials in certain bases. For example, a basis for the even polynomials of degrees 1 to 4 follows:
degree 1: 2a - b - c
degree 2: 2a^2 - b^2 - c^2, 2bc - ca - ab
degree 3: 2a^3 - b^3 - c^3, a^2b + a^2c - b^2c - b^2c, a^2b + a^2c - b^2c - b^2c
A basis for the odd polynomials of degrees 1 to 2 follows:
degree 1: b - c
degree 2: (b - c)(a + b + c), (b - c)a
See Clark Kimberling, "A combinatorial classification of triangle centers on the line at infinity," Journal of Integer Sequences 22 (2019) Article 19.5.4.

families.title: Collings Transforms
p: If ABC is a triangle, P is a point, and A', B', C' are the reflections of A, B, C in P, then the circumcircles of triangles AB'C', A'BC' and A'B'C concur at a point Q on the circumcircle of triangle ABC. The transformation T given by Q = T(P) was described by S. N. Collings, "Reflections on reflections 2", Mathematical Gazette 1974, page 264.

It was further discussed by Floor van Lamoen and Darij Grinberg, and coordinates were found by Barry Wolk; see Hyacinthos #4547, #4548, #6469, #6538, #6546, #6560. Paul Yiu noted that T(P) is the point, other than A, B, C, in which the circumconic centered at P meets the circumcircle of triangle ABC (#4548).
If P = x : y : z (trilinears), then Q = f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b), where
f(a,b,c) = 1/[bz(ax + by - cz) - cy(ax + cz - by)].
For given Q, the set of points P satisfying T(P) = Q is a conic. Examples follow:
if Q = X(74), the conic passes through X(i) for I = 125;
if Q = X(98), the conic passes through X(i) for I = 115, 868;
if Q = X(100), the conic passes through X(i) for I = 1, 9, 10, 119, 142, 214, 442, 1145;
if Q = X(107), the conic passes through X(i) for I = 4, 133, 800, 1249;
if Q = X(110), the conic passes through X(i) for I = 5, 6, 113, 141, 206, 942, 960, 1147, 1209;
if Q = X(476), the conic passes through X(i) for I = 30.

families.title: Brisse Transforms
p: Suppose that P is a point on the circumcircle Γ of triangle ABC. Let U and V be the lines through P tangent to the incircle. Line U meets Γ in a point U' other than P, and line V meets Γ in a point V' other than P. The line U'V' is tangent to the incircle. The touchpoint, denoted by T(P), is the Brisse transform of P. Suppose P is given by barycentrics u : v : w. Barycentrics for T(P) are found in Edward Brisse, Perspective Poristic Triangles: a^4/[(b + c - a)u^2] : b^4/[(c + a - b)v^2] : c^4/[(a + b - c)w^2].
If X is given by trilinears x : y : z, then T(X) has trilinears a/[(b + c - a)x^2] : b/[(c + a - b)y^2] : c/[(a + b - c)z^2].
Examples: X(11) = Feuerbach point = T(X(109))
X(1317) = incircle-antipode of X(11) = T(X(106))

Still open is the question posed in Hyacinthos #6832: to list all polynomial centers on the incircle having low degree and to prove that there are no others. Here, "degree" of X = p(a,b,c) : p(b,c,a) : p(c,a,b) [barycentrics] refers to the degree of homogeneity of p(a,b,c), and "low" means less than 6. (The Feuerbach point, X(11), has degree 3.)
In Hyacinthos #6835, Paul Yiu gives two methods for constructing polynomial centers on the incircle:
(1) If X is a polynomial center on the incircle and W is any other polynomial center, then the line XW meets the incircle in another point that is a polynomial center.
(2) If W is on the line at infinity, then the barycentric square W^2 is on the Steiner inscribed ellipse, and the barycentric product X(7)*W^2 is on the incircle.

families.title: Beth Conjugates
p: If X is a triangle center then X = P-beth conjugate of P for some triangle center P. Using the definition of beth conjugate (in the Glossary), it is easy to prove that the P-beth conjugate of P is the trilinear product P*X(56),
so that P = X*X(8). In trilinears, if P = p : q : r, then (P-beth conjugate of P) = up : vq : wr, where
u : v : w = a/(b + c - a) : b/(c + a - b) : c/(a + b - c), or equivalently,
u : v : w = 1 - cos A : 1 - cos B : 1 - cos C.

families.title: Orthojoins
p: The orthojoin of a point X = x : y : z other than X(6) is defined in the Glossary algebraically in terms of variables a,b,c. When these are sidelengths of a triangle, orthojoin(X) is the orthopole of the trilinear polar of the isogonal conjugate of X. (Added to ETC 6/18/03.) Let D(a,b,c) = bc[2abcx + c^3y + b^3z - bc(by + cz) - a^2(cy + bz)],
E(a,b,c) = [(a^4 - (b^2 - c^2)^2]x - 4a^2bc(y cos B + z cos C),
f(a,b,c) = D(a,b,c)E(a,b,c).
Then orthojoin(X) = f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b). Below, orthojoin(X) is written as H(X).
Suppose X is not X(2) and does not lie on a sideline of triangle ABC. The crossdifference of X and X(2) has first trilinear
a(b-c)x', where x' = (by - cz)/(b-c).
Let X ^-1 denote the isogonal conjugate of X. Then
H(X ^-1) = (by - cz) cos A : (cz - ax) cos B : (ax - by) cos C.

In other words, if X lies on a line PG through the centroid G, then H(X ^-1) lies on the line HQ, where H denotes the orthocenter and Q is a point that can be determined from the above formula. Examples:
If X is on the Euler line, L(2,3), then H(X ^-1) is on the line L(4,6);
If X is on L(2,6,), then H(X ^-1) is on the Euler line;
If X is on L(1,2), then H(X ^-1) is on L(4,9);
If X is on L(2,7), then H(X ^-1) is on L(1,4).
Suppose P is not X(6), and let
S = crossdifference(P, X(6)) (S lies on the line at infinity)
S' = orthopoint(S) (S' lies on the line at infinity)
S" = complementary conjugate of S' (S" lies on the nine-point circle)
Let X be a point on line PX(6) and not on a sideline of ABC. Then H(X ^-1) is on line S"S'. Examples:

families.title: TCC Perspectors
p: Suppose P is a point. As noted in TCCT, p. 201, the tangential triangle is perspective to the circumcevian triangle of P. (The tangential triangle is also perspector to the circum-anticevian triangle of P, with the same perspector as for the circumcevian triangle of P.) In August 2003, Jean-Pierre Ehrmann gave barycentrics for the perspector, called the TCC-perspector of P. For further properties of TCC perpsectors, published some 14 years after their introduction here, see I. Minevich and P. Morton, International Journal of Geometry 2017, "Synthetic foundations of cevian geometry, IV"

p: contributed by Darij Grinberg, August 24, 2003.

families.title: Circle-related points

families.title: Mimosa transforms and inverse Mimosa tranforms
p: contributed by Clark Kimberling, September 16, 2003. Let g(P,X) denote the P-gimel conjugate of X. The Mimosa transform M(X) arises in connection with the equation g(P,X) = X.

families.title: Zozma transforms
p: (isogonal conjugates of inverse Mimosa transforms)

families.title: Centers from bicentric pairs
p: Suppose P and U are a bicentric pair. Many operations on P and U result in triangle centers. Among these are trilinear and barycentric product, bicentric sum, bicentric difference, crosssum, and crossdifference.

families.title: Orthocorrespondents
p: Suppose that P is a point in the plane of triangle ABC. The perpendiculars through P to the lines AP, BP, CP meet the lines BC, CA, AB, respectively, in collinear points. Let L denote their line. The trilinear pole of L is the orthocorrespondent of P. This definition was introduced by Bernard Gibert.

families.title: Gallatly circle
p: (pedal cicle of the 1st and 2nd Brocard points).

families.title: Euler-Vecten-Gibert Points
p: On August 13, 2003, Bernard Gibert contributed six centers that lie on the Euler line and are related to the Vecten points.

families.title: Orion transforms
p: contributed by Jean-Peirre Ehramann, September 24, 2003.

families.title: Inverses in circumcircle
p: contributed by Peter Moses.

families.title: PK and NK Transforms
p: contributed by Bernard Gibert, October 1, 2003. Let X ^-1 denote the isogonal conjugate of X. Then PK(X) is the point of intersection of the trilinear polar of X and the trilinear polar of X ^-1, and NK(P) is the pole of the line XX^-1 with respect to the conic that passes through points A, B, C, X, and X ^-1. Also, PK(X) is the crossdifference, and NK(X) the crosssum, of X and X ^-1.

families.title: Reflections
p: contributed by Peter Moses.

families.title: points on the 2nd equal-areas cubic, EAC2
p: For any point P on EAC2, the X(2)-isoconjugate of P is also on EAC2. Contributed by Clark Kimberling.

families.title: Eigencenters and eigentransforms
p: Contributed by Clark Kimberling, October, 2003.

families.title: More points on the circumcircle
p: October 20, 2003, revised January 20, 2015 following suggestions by Viktor Kataysky. Notations: CIR(U)

families.title: Gibert-Simson Transforms
p: On October 19, 2003, Bernard Gibert contributed points that lie on the Simson cubic. Indeed, this cubic is the image of the circumcircle under a mapping here named the Gibert-Simson transform.

families.title: (Mostly) circle-related points
p: contributed by Peter J. C. Moses, October-November, 2003. See the notes just before X(1662) for an introduction and notation. Included in this section are centers of similitude of several pairs of circles.

families.title: related to bicentric pairs
p: Most of the centers X(2594) - X(2670) are defined in terms of bicentric pairs of points (e.g., the 1st and 2nd Brocard points).
For a list of bicentric pairs and associated terminology and properties, press the Tables button at the top of this page.

families.title: Rigby-Simson points and Simson-Rigby points
p: Centers X(2677) to X(2770) are examples of Rigby-Simson points and Simson-Rigby points. These two types of points are discussed in
Ross Honsberger, Episodes in Nineteenth and Twentieth Century Euclidean Geometry, Mathematical Association of America, 1995. Chapter 11: The Orthopole, pages 124-136.

Specifically, on pages 132-136, Honsberger defines the "Rigby Point," in honor of John Rigby, as the orthopole of the six sides of two triangles, all of whose vertices lie on a circle, and he notes that this orthopole lies on the six Simson lines of the vertices.

Now suppose that P = p : q : r (trilinears) and U = u : v : w are distinct points on the circumcircle of a triangle ABC. Their Simson lines meet in a point X which is here called the Rigby-Simson point of P and U, denoted by RS(P,U). That is, RS(P,U) is the orthopole of line PU with respect to triangle ABC.

On the circumcircle, there is a unique point K whose Simson line is perpendicular to line PU, and whose Simson line also passes through RS(P,U). The point K is here called the Simson-Rigby point of P and U, denoted by SR(P,U). Note that SR(P,U) = Λ(P,U)
If you have The Geometer's Sketchpad, you can view RS(P,U) and SR(P,U).
Continuing with contributions of Peter Moses during October, 2004, trilinears for RS(P,U) are
f(a,b,c,p,q,r,u,v,w) : f(b,c,a,q,r,p,v,w,u) : f(c,a,b,r,p,q,w,u,v), where
f(a,b,c,p,q,r,u,v,w) = 1/[a^2r^2v^2(q cos A - p cos B)(w cos A - u cos C)] - 1/[a^2q^2w^2(r cos A - p cos C)(v cos A - u cos B)],
and trilinears for SR(P,U), reckoned as the point of intersection of lines P-to-U ^- 1 and U-to-P ^- 1, are

families.title: Simson-Moses points
p: defined by changing "isogonal" to "isotomic" in the definition of Simson-Ribgy points (X(2687)-X(2770).

families.title: Isogonal Conjugates with respect to Special Triangles
p: (e.g,, medial, orthic, excentral, tangential). The term "complementary conjugate" already in use at the time of this writing (November 11, 2004) is a synonym for "medial isogonal conjugate", as is "anticomplementary conjugate" for "anticomplementary isogonal conjugate"; accordingly, the earlier terms will be used in the sequel. Also, "excentral isogonal conjugate" is "X(188)-aleph conjugate" and "orthic isogonal conjugate" is "X(4)-Ceva conjugate"; in these cases, the new terminology will be used.

families.title: Points lying on the MacBeath inconic
p: contributed by Peter Moses, November 12, 2004,

families.title: Dual triangles: DC points and CD points
p: contributed by Clark Kimberling. Suppose DEF is a triangle in the plane of triangle ABC. Let D' be the isogonal conjugate of the point of intersection of line EF and the line at infinity. Define E' and F' cyclically. The triangle D'E'F' is here named the dual of DEF. The vertices of D'E'F' lie on the circumcircle, and D'E'F' is similar to DEF. The duality is between the sidelines EF, FD, DE and the points D', E', F', respectively. For example, if E and F remain fixed and D varies, then D' remains fixed, while E'F' varies. Actually D'E'F' is the dual of any triangle homothetic to DEF. Indeed, DEF need not be a triangle but can be the union of three concurrent lines. Suppose U is a point having cevian triangle DEF and dual triangle D'E'F'. Then there exists a point DC(U) whose circum-anticevian triangle (TCCT, p. 201) is D'E'F'. To construct DC(U) from U, let A' = AD'∩BC, and let A" be the {B,C}-harmonic conjugate of A'. Define B" and C" cyclically. The lines AA", BB", CC" concur in DC(U). Also, DC(U) = U-isoconjugate of the crosssum of U and X(6).

families.title: Intersections of Central Lines
p: This section presents points X(3000) to X(3019) of intersection of lines listed in MathWorld's Central Line. Contributed by Eric Weisstein, December, 2004.

families.title: Antipodal Pairs on Circles
p: In response to Stevanovic's findings (X(3000) to X(3006)), Peter Moses noted (Hyacinthos, 12/9/2004) a method for mapping a pair of antipodal points on one circle to an antipodal pair on another circle. The method depends on centers of similitude: Suppose O_1 and O_2 are circles, that P is on O_1 and that P' is the antipode of P on O_1. Let U be the internal center of similitude (insimilicenter) of O_1 and O_2, and V the exsimilicenter. Define Q = PU ∩P' V and Q' = PV ∩P' U. Then on O_2, point Q' is the antipode of Q. Moreover, the lines PP' and QQ' are parallel.

families.title: Centers X(3112)-X(3118)
p: represent points introduced by Quang Tuan Bui in Hyacinthos, August 5, 2006. Suppose X is a point not on a sideline of ABC. Let
gX = isogonal conjugate of X
tX = isotomic conjugate of X
tgX = isotomic conjugate of gX
gtX = isogonal conjugate of tX
Gt = intersection of lines X(tX) and (gX)(gtX)
Tg = intersection of lines X(gX) and (tX)(tgX)

Then the points A, B, C, gX, tX, Tg, Gt are on a conic. As a circumconic, it is the image under the isogonal conjugate mapping of line X(gtX). It is also the image under the isotomic conjugate mapping of line X(tgX).

families.title: Danneels Perspectors
p: Suppose A_1B_1C_1 is the cevian triangle of a point X. Let L_AB be the line through B parallel to A_1B_1, and let L_AC be the line through C parallel to A_1C_1.
Let A_2 = L_AB∩L_AC, and define B_2 and C_2 cyclically. Let

Eric Danneels proves in "A Simple Perspectivity," Forum Geometricorum 6 (2006) 199-203, that the triangles A_3B_3C_3 and ABC are perspective. If X = x : y : z (barycentrics), then the Danneels perspector P(X) is given by

families.title: are associated with six equilateral triangles
p: related to the (1st) Morley triangle; trilinears for vertices of these triangles are given just below. Received from Milorad R. Stevanovic, November 24, 2007 and December 25, 2007.

families.title: Barycentric Products of Perpendicular Directions
p: Suppose P and U are points on the line at infinity, given in barycentric coordinates by P = p : q : r and U = u : v : w. We call P and U perpendicular directions if for every point X not in the line at infinity, the lines XP and XU are perpendicular. (It is well known that if P and U are an antipodal pair on the circumcircle, then their isogonal conjugates are perpendicular directions.)

families.title: Incircle transforms
p: Suppose that U = u : v : w (trilinears) is a point other than the symmedian point, X(6). The incircle transform of U is the point T(U) = a (a - b + c) (a + b - c) (c v - b w)^2 : : , which lies on the incircle. Geometrically, T(U) is the Brisse transform of the psi transform of X(6) and U. (Brisse transform is described just before X(1254), and psi transform, also called the "Psi mapping" elsewhere in ETC, and TCCT, p. 80, is defined in the preamble just before X(98).

families.title: Vertex conjugates
p: Suppose that U = u : v : w and X = x : y : z (trilinears) are points not on a sideline of ABC. Let f(a,b,c) = a/[a^2vwyz - ux(bw + cv)(bz + cy)]. The U-vertex conjugate of X is the point f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b). For a geometric interpretation, let T be the vertex triangle of the circumcevian triangles, A_UB_UC_U and A_XB_XC_X, of U and X; viz., the sidelines of T are A_UA_X, B_UB_X, C_UC_X. Then T is perspective to ABC, and the perspector is the U-vertex conjugate of X.

families.title: Points associated with Morley cubics K29, K30, K31
p: Points X(3602)-X(3609) are associated with the three Morley Cubics indexed as K29, K30, K31 at Bernard Gibert's Cubics in the Triangle Plane. The points are related to those in the section just before X(3272), under the heading "Points Associated with Equilateral Triangles." See also
Jean-Pierre Ehrmann and Bernard Gibert, "A Morley Configuration," Forum Geometricorum 1 (2001) 51-58. (Click here to download a PDF of this article.)

families.title: Homothetic centers
p: Suppose that X is a triangle center, that M is the medial triangle, and that t is a real number. The t-dilation of M from X, denoted by H(X; M, t), is a triangle center. If X = x : y : z (trilinears), then
with inverse given by
H^-1(X; M, t) = bc[(1 - t)(by + cz) - 2ax] : ca[(1 - t)(cz + ax) - 2by : ab[(1 - t)(ax + by) - 2cz].
César E. Lozada contributed several such triangle centers (March 21, 2011).

families.title: Kirikami-Schiffler Points
p: Suppose that X is a point and A'B'C' is a central triangle. Let L_A be the line through A' parallel to the Euler line of triangle BCX, let L_B be the line through B' parallel to the Euler line of CXA, and let L_C be the line through C' parallel to the Euler line of AXB. It is well known that if X=X(1), the incenter, then the three aforementioned Euler lines concur in the Schiffler point, X(21). If their parallels, the lines L_A, L_B, L_C concur, the point of concurrence is the Kirikami-Schiffler point of the triangle A'B'C', denoted by KS(A'B'C'). Seiichi Kirikami (February 1, 2011) found that those lines concur if A'B'C' is the reference triangle ABC and also concur if A'B'C' is the medial triangle. Peter Moses found additional cases and properties..

families.title: Central Triangles and More Combos
p: Many triangle centers can be defined (as just above) by the form Xcom(nT), where T denotes a central triangle. In order to present such centers, it is helpful to introduce the notation T(f(a,b,c), g(b,c,a)) for central triangles. (This lengthly preamble was completed December 23, 2011.)

families.title: More Combos. Continuing the discussion of points Xcom(T)
p: suppose that T is an arbitrary triangle, and let nT denote the normalization of T. Let NT denote the set of these triangles, as matrices, and let * denote matrix multiplication. Then NT is closed under *. Also, NT is closed under matrix inversion. Consequently, (NT, *) is a group, comparable to the group of stochastic matrices. Suppose that T_1 and T_2 are triangles. In many cases, the product T_1*T_2 is well-defined (e.g., TCCT, page 175). However, n(T_1*T_2) may not be n(T_1)*n(T_2) if T_1 and T_2 are not normalized. Therefore, it is important, when dealing with products, to include the "n" if it is intended.

families.title: Central Triangles and More Combos
p: (See just above, Centers X(3663)-X(3861).

families.title: Inverse Triangles and More Combos
p: The Euler triangle and the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th Euler triangles are discussed in the preamble to X(3758), along with eight other central triangles using the notation T(f(a,b,c), g(b,c,a)). Recall that the inverse of a normalized central triangle T, denoted by Inverse(nT) or Inverse(n(T)), is also a normalized central triangle. Barycentrics for the inverse of each of the 13 triangles and properties of these triangles were given (Peter Moses, December 2011).

families.title: Points on the Euler line
p: Many points are found as points of intersection of the Euler line and other central lines.

families.title: Points on the Brocard Axis
p: Many points are found as points of intersection of the Brocard Axis and other central lines.

families.title: Points on the Soddy Line
p: Many points are found as points of intersection of the Soddy Line and other central lines.

families.title: More Central Triangles and Combos
p: This section consists of points of the form X(k)com[T(f(a,b,c),g(b,c,a)], for choices of the pairs (f(a,b,c), g(b,c,a)) as indicated in the following list:
T(a, c), T(-a, c), T(a, b - c), T(a, c - b), T(a^2, bc), T(-a^2, bc), T(bc, bc + c^2), T(-bc, bc + c^2), T(bc, b^2 + bc), T(-bc, b^2 + bc) )
For notation and precedents, see the preambles just before X(3748) and X(3862).

families.title: Walsmith Points
p: Early in 2012, Russell Walsmith introduced this point and conjectured that it lies on the Euler line. Peter Moses found barycentrics for the point and its inverse-in-the-circumcircle, X(5001), and proved that the two points lie on the Euler line.

families.title: Points on the Hutson-Moses hyperbola
p: The Hutson-Moses hyperbola, introduced at X(5375), is given by the following barycentric equation:
a(a - b)(a - c)yz + b(b - c)(b - a)zx + c(c - a)(c - b)xy = 0.

This hyperbola has perspector X(100), center X(5375), meets the circumcircle in X(898) and the Steiner circumellipse in X(666), and is the isogonal conjugate of the line X(244)X(665). If X = x : y : z (barycentrics) is a point on the circumcircle, then the point H(X) = x/(a(b - c)) : y/(b(c - a)) : z/(c(a - b)) is on the Hutson-Moses hyperbola.

families.title: Isogonal Conjugates With Respect To Various Triangles
p: Many triangle centers are constructible as isogonal conjugates with respect to a central triangle T other than ABC. See, for example, the preamble to X(2883). Other examples are X(5642), for which T is the Thomson triangle, and X(5957), for which T is the Feuerbach triangle. In the latter case, a long formula for barycentric coordinates is given for the Feuerbach isogonal conjugate of an arbitrary point p : q : r is given. Peter Moses (August 11, 2014) developed a much longer formula for the isogonal conjugate of a point p : q : r with respect to a triangle having vertices d1 : d2 : d3, e1 : e2 : e3, f1 : f2 : f3. The total number of characters in the formula is (pending). Although too long to be stated here, the formula served as a basis for finding triangle centers X(i) for i = 6000-6030.

For well-established central triangles T, (e.g., Thomson, Feuerbach, intouch, extouch), the phrase "isogonal conjugate with respect to T can be shortened to "T isogonal conjugate" or "T-I C″, as in many of the next triangle centers.

It T is a triangle, then T-isogonal conjugation carries points on the circumcircle of T to the line at infinity. For example, taking T = Brocard triangle, the appearance of (X(i),X(j)) in the following list means that T-I C of X(i) is X(j): (3,2782), (6,804), (1083,2795), (1316,690), (5091,2787), (5108,543).

families.title: Lozada Perspectors
p: Suppose that A′B′C′ be the cevian triangle of a point P. Let L be the line through A′ tangent to the incircle, and let A* be the touchpoint; define B* and C* cyclically. Then A*B*C* is perspective to ABC for all P. (César Lozada, May 7, 2014, Anopolis #1466)
If P = p : q : r (trilinears), then the perspector is P* = a(b + c - a)p^2 : b(a + c - b)q^2 : c(a + b - c)r^2.

families.title: Points Associated with the Steiner Deltoid
p: Suppose that ABC is a triangle. Its Steiner deltoid, SD, is the envelope of the Simson lines of ABC. Peter Moses (September 14, 2014) defined a mapping from (O) to SD; the mapping is here denoted by M and named the Moses-Steiner image.

families.title: the Dao-Moses-Telv Circle and Associated Points
p: The Dao-Moses-Telv circle is defined as the circle passing through these six points:
F_1 = X(13), the 1st Fermat point
F_2 = X(14), the 2nd Fermat point
F_3 = inverse of F_1 in the circumcircle
F_4 = inverse of F_2 in the circumcircle
F_5 = inverse of F_1 in the nine-point circle
F_6 = inverse of F_2 in the nine-point circle

Dao Thanh Oai noted that these points are concyclic, Telv Cohl gave a proof, and Peter Moses discovered properties described in this preamble. The center of the Dao-Moses-Telv circle is X(1637). (Francisco Javier García Capitán, November 3, 2014)

The Dao-Moses-Telv circle is orthogonal to the circumcircle, the nine-point circle, and all the other circles in their coaxal family. The circle passes through X(5000) and X(5001), these being the Walsmith point and its inverse in the circumcircle. (Peter Moses, November 6, 2014)

families.title: Moses Radical Circle and Associated Points
p: Summarizing notes from Peter Moses (November 7, 2014), the circle here named the Moses radical circle, MRC, is defined as the radical circle of the circumcircle, nine-point circle, and Brocard circle. The center of MRC is X(647), and, like the Dao-Moses-Telv circle (see X(6103), MRC passes through X(5000) and X(5001).

families.title: Centers of Circles Orthogonal to the Coaxal System of the Circumcircle and Nine-Point Circle
p: Continuing Peter Moses's discussion in the preamble to X(6112)-X)6128), suppose that P = p : q : r (barycentrics) is a point other than the circumcenter. Let U(P) be the circle that passes through P and its circumcircle-inverse and is orthogonal to the coaxal system of the circumcircle and nine-point circle. Then X(5000) and X(5001) lie on U

families.title: Centers of Circles Orthogonal to the Coaxal System of the Circumcircle and Brocard Circle
p: Continuing Peter Moses's discussion in the preambles to X(6112) and X(6129), suppose that P = p : q : r (barycentrics) is a point other than the circumcenter. Let V(P) be the circle that passes through P and its circumcircle-inverse and is orthogonal to the Schoute coaxal system; that is, the coaxal system of the circumcircle and Brocard circle. Then X(15) and X(16) lie on V, and the center of V is the point M(V) = f(a,b,c) : f(b,c,a) : f(c,a,b) given by . . .

families.title: and X(6600)-XX(6661), Symbolic Substitution
p: contributed by Clark Kimberling, August 8, 2026. The notation "SS(a → S_A)" denotes barycentric symbolic substitution, similar to trilinear symbolic substitution defined at X(3221). Symbolic substitution carries lines to lines, conics to conics, and cubics to cubics. For example, since X(1), X(2), X(3), X(4), X(6), X(9), X(57), X(1073), X(1249) lie on the Thomson cubic, their images under SS(a →S_A) lie on the cubic given by
The subject of symbolic substitution was introduced in C. Kimberling, "Symbolic substitutions in the transfigured plane of a triangle," Aequationes Mathematicae 73 (2007) 156-171.
